formation.note: No fetched source states an explicit collaboration formation date. Wikipedia states data collection commenced 2018-04-01, but as a rank-12 source it may not be the sole source of a critical value, so no formation date is asserted.

intervals.label: collaboration
intervals.note: Start is conservatively taken from the confirmed 2023 relocation to Leibstadt rather than the unconfirmed ~2018 Brokdorf start (Wikipedia only); the collaboration in fact operated CONUS at Brokdorf earlier, but that start date is not sourced to a primary publication, so no earlier date is asserted.
intervals.quote: In 2023, the Conus setup moved to another power plant in Leibstadt, Switzerland (KKL), since the reactor at KBR stopped operation

name: CONUS / CONUS+ Collaboration
notes: host_facility_id/host_site_id record the current (Leibstadt) location; the collaboration operated at facility:brokdorf-nuclear-power-plant from 2018-2023 (see experiment:conus facility_roles).
No official collaboration page with an institution/member count was found reachable (checked 2026-09-17); membership fields are left null rather than estimated from author lists on papers.

The CONUS+ overview paper (arXiv:2407.11912) names the Max-Planck-Institut fur Kernphysik (MPIK) as the institution with the direct real-time network connection to the experiment, and other CONUS papers list co-authors from KIT, Duke University, PSI and the plant operators, but no single source consulted gives an authoritative institution count or list. No institution-level member list is recorded in the Atlas.

summary.plain: The physicists who built and run the CONUS and CONUS+ reactor-neutrino experiments, led from the Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics in Germany.
summary.technical: CONUS/CONUS+ collaboration, anchored at the Max-Planck-Institut fur Kernphysik (MPIK) Heidelberg with co-authors from institutions including KIT, Duke University and PSI on its publications; no official member/institution count located.
